openings.claim: Compare existing anonymous lot-by-shift summaries: a lot explanation predicts persistence across shifts; a process explanation predicts persistence across lots within the implicated shift.
openings.discriminator: Comparable crossed cells showing the opposite pattern defeat the corresponding prediction; confounded coverage cannot discriminate.
openings.probe: Inspect crossed coverage using existing records only, disclose no employee identities, and retain absent cells and missing values without imputation. Report non-identifiability if coverage is confounded.
openings.uncertainty: Synthetic proposal only; no records, defect measurements, or causal findings supplied. Coverage and comparability are unknown.

openings.claim: Collect deliberately crossed new samples to expose differences hidden by existing lot-shift assignments; this predicts improved separability, not a winning cause.
openings.discriminator: Continued inseparability defeats the proposed sampling advantage.
openings.probe: Do not execute unless existing-records-only is explicitly relaxed and sampling resources obtained; then assess separability while protecting identities and preserving missingness.
openings.uncertainty: No sampling budget supplied; access, expense, and discriminatory yield remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves the comparison operation, competing persistence predictions, and coverage stopping gate.
Preserves crossing-dependent separability as an explicitly gated alternative.

decision: Start with D1 coverage inspection. Discriminate only if comparable crossed records support it; otherwise report non-identifiability. D2 requires constraint relaxation and resources. Reject imputation. No causal winner is established.
